newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania and Moldova to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: Romania and Moldova to boost ties.

text.p: The leaders of Romania and the ex-Soviet republic of Moldova declared on Monday they would work to boost ties but ruled out a formal merger between the two countries which share a common language.

"It is hard to imagine the development of Moldova outside the context of its relations with Romania," Moldovan president- elect Petru Lucinschi told reporters after talks with President Emil Constantinescu in Bucharest.

Lucinschi arrived in Romania for a short visit on Monday, his first official trip abroad since he won a four-year term on a centre-left ticket last month. He will take over from Moldova's President Mircea Snegur on January 15.
Moldova is made up mostly of the territory of Bessarabia taken from Romania by Moscow under a 1939 Nazi-Soviet pact.
Nearly two-thirds of its residents are ethnic Romanians and the two countries share a common language.

Constantinescu, who won a presidential election himself last month, also affirmed his commitment to cement ties with Moldova saying the two states should promote "closer relations, strongly based on the economic cooperation."
"We must overcome the stage of statements. We have identified a series of blockages in our relations," Constantinescu told reporters.
He added that a joint commission of experts was expected to complete a report highlighting new ways to develop ties between the two neighbour states.

Constantinescu said he had discussed with Lucinschi plans to create free trade zones along the border to smooth border traffic and build several bridges across the River Prut which forms a natural border.

Asked whether he would favour a German-style merger of Moldova with Romania, Lucinschi said the issue should be placed within the "European context where the historical aspect of the problem should prevail."
"We are two states which live in friendship and have the same language and culture. We can continue the process of integration and cooperation within a united Europe," he said.
Recreating the "Greater Romania" of the early 20th century was a hot issue in both countries after the end of Soviet rule. But it has largely died down in both Romania and Moldova.
Romania has yet to sign friendship treaties with Moldova and with the ex-Soviet republics -- Ukraine and Russia -- which reject its demand for a public apology over the 1939 pact.
The treaties are seen as vital for Romania's ambition to join the European Union and NATO.
"Nothing has happened yet with the treaty. We still have to work on it," Lucinschi said.
